questions.question: Generally, in India population census is conducted after how many years?

questions.solution: Population census in India is conducted every 10 years to gather comprehensive demographic, social, and economic data. questions.question: The Indian census is generally held every ________.
questions.questionHtml: The Indian census is generally held every ________.
questions.solution: The Indian census is conducted every tenth year as per the provisions of the Census Act, 1948, and the Constitution of India. All censuses since 1951 have been conducted under this act. The most recent census was conducted in 2011, which was the seventh census in independent India. The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, conduct the census. The first complete census was conducted in 1881, and the concept of the census was started by British Viceroy Lord Mayo in 1872.

questions.question: According to the 2011 Census, the literacy rate among females in India is _________ compared to males.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is lower.

Key Points

  • According to the Census 2011, the literacy rate among females in India was 65.46%, compared to 82.14% for males.
  • The gap in literacy rates between males and females highlights gender disparity in education.
  • States like Kerala have a higher female literacy rate, while states like Bihar and Rajasthan lag behind.
  • Government initiatives such as Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan aim to bridge this literacy gap.

Additional Information

  • Literacy Rate:
    • Defined as the percentage of the population aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding.
    • Measured during the decennial Census in India.

    • Factors such as traditional societal norms, early marriage, and lack of access to education contribute to the lower literacy rate among females.
    • Efforts are being made to ensure equal educational opportunities for all genders.
  • Government Schemes to Improve Female Literacy:
    • Beti Bachao Beti Padhao: Focuses on promoting education among girls and preventing gender-biased sex-selective elimination.
    • Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan: Aims to provide holistic education, including quality education for girls.
  • Global Comparison:
    • India's female literacy rate is lower compared to global averages, which emphasize the need for sustained efforts.

    • Education is another significant factor for migration, especially among the younger population seeking higher education in urban centers.

questions.question: The density of population in India (Census 2011) is __________________ persons per sq km.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 382.

  • The density of population in India is calculated by dividing the total population of India by the total area of the country.
  • As per the 2011 Census, the total population of India was 1.21 billion and the total area was 3.17 million sq km.
  • Therefore, the density of population in India in 2011 was 382 persons/sq km.

questions.question: In the context of the Indian census, what is the definition of the literacy percentage?

options.text: The percentage of people aged seven and above, who can read and write in any language
options.html: The percentage of people aged seven and above, who can read and write in any language

options.text: The percentage of people with a college degree
options.html: The percentage of people with a college degree

questions.solution: The literacy rate in the Indian census measures the proportion of individuals aged seven and above who possess basic reading and writing skills in any language. This age criterion is chosen because children typically begin schooling by this age, acquiring fundamental literacy skills. Literacy is distinct from having a college degree or advanced education, and it encompasses all languages, reflecting India's multilingual context.

    • It typically includes data on demographics, economic activities, education, and housing conditions.
    • The census is usually conducted every 10 years in most countries.
    • In India, the Census of India is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
  • Importance of Census Data
    • Census data is crucial for government planning and policy-making.
    • It helps in the allocation of resources and development of infrastructure.
    • The data is used for electoral constituency delimitation.
    • It provides insights into the socio-economic conditions of the population.
  • Challenges in Conducting Census
    • Ensuring complete coverage and accuracy can be challenging due to the vast and diverse population.
    • Remote and inaccessible areas pose logistical difficulties.
    • Ensuring data privacy and security is critical.
    • There can be issues with data collection due to lack of cooperation or awareness among the population.
  • Technological Advancements in Census
    • Recent censuses have incorporated technology for data collection and processing.
    • Use of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for mapping and analysis.
    • Digital data collection methods to improve accuracy and efficiency.
    • Real-time data monitoring and validation to ensure reliability.

questions.question: The number of organisms in the population divided by a regular unit of area or volume is called ______.
questions.questionHtml: The number of organisms in the population divided by a regular unit of area or volume is called ______.
questions.solution: Population density refers to the number of organisms in a population divided by a regular unit of area or volume. It is a key metric in ecology, crucial for understanding species distribution and abundance, resource competition, and urban planning. High density increases competition, while low density may pose challenges in resource access and mate finding.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, India’s population accounts _________ of the world’s population.
questions.questionHtml: According to Census 2011, India’s population accounts _________ of the world’s population.
questions.solution: The 2011 Census of India reported a population of over 1.2 billion, accounting for 17.5% of the world's population. The gender ratio was 940 females per 1,000 males. Urban population increased to 31.16% from 27.81% in 2001. Literacy rates were 74.04% overall, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%. Scheduled Castes and Tribes made up 16.6% and 8.6% of the population, respectively. Uttar Pradesh was the most populous state, while Sikkim was the least.

questions.question: Census in India was first started under ________ in the year 1872.
questions.questionHtml: Census in India was first started under ________ in the year 1872.
questions.solution: Lord Mayo was the Viceroy of India from 1869 to 1872, and he introduced the first regular census in India in 1872. The census was conducted to collect data on population, literacy, religion, and occupation, among other things, to assist the colonial government in policymaking and resource allocation.

questions.questionHtml: As per Census 2011, which of the following union territories of India has the lowest population?
questions.solution: Lakshadweep, as per Census 2011. Sikkim is the smallest state and Lakshadweep is the smallest union territory in India on the basis of population. questions.question: According to census 2011, the only Indian state having negative decadal population growth rate between 2001-11 is _______.
questions.questionHtml: According to census 2011, the only Indian state having negative decadal population growth rate between 2001-11 is _______.
questions.solution: Nagaland, as per Census 2011, is the only Indian state with negative decadal population growth (-0.5%) between 2001-11. Comparatively, Goa, Uttarakhand, and Sikkim had positive growth rates. Nagaland, in Northeast India, is culturally rich with tribal diversity, bordered by Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, and Myanmar, featuring Kohima as its capital.
